sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Kalmia microphylla is a low shrub of western North America, usually 5–80 cm tall. It grows in alpine meadows, bogs and other wet soils.

sections.title: Leaves and flowers
sections.text: Its opposite leaves are about 1.5–4 cm long and 0.3–1.2 cm wide. Pink to purple flowers appear in small clusters and produce capsules.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: Like other Kalmia, this species contains grayanotoxins; livestock poisoning is documented. The sources consulted do not specify effects in people, so do not eat the leaves, flowers or fruits.
